title: agent-system project configuration
description: Drop this at <repo>/.claude/agent-system.json to opt a project into the agent-system. Absence of this file means the project is not opted in: hooks stay silent and the commit guard never fires.

project.description: Short project name, used as the event-log key and the dashboard title.

worktreesDir.description: Directory holding the fixed worktrees. Each is auto-named `lane<N>` by `lanes new` (N = max existing + 1) — the number is baked into the directory name at creation time, so it stays stable across add/remove; it is never recomputed from position. Supports ~ expansion. This is only the DEFAULT: `lanes worktrees-dir <path>` sets a per-machine override in the gitignored `.claude/agent-system.local.json`, which wins over this field whenever present (useful when teammates want their lanes on different disks). `lanes adopt` writes new values there, never here. Omit this (and basePort) if the repo does not use worktrees: lanes are disabled, `lanes status` falls back to whatever sessions appear in the log, and everything else still works.

basePort.description: Dev-server port prefix, purely informational — nothing starts a server for you. Lane N is shown as serving on `${basePort}${N}` (basePort 300 -> lane 2 is 3002). This is only the DEFAULT: `lanes base-port <n>` sets a per-machine override in the gitignored `.claude/agent-system.local.json`, same file and same precedence as `worktreesDir`.

commands.description: Project commands. /gate runs the gates once at the end; the reviewer never runs them. A command left null is a gate that is skipped, and /gate says so.

pattern.description: Regex whose first all-digits capture group is the issue number. Default: ^[a-z]+/(\d+)-

prefixes.description: Branch prefix -> issue label. null means no label.

base.description: Base branch new work branches off, and the reference for ahead/behind and free-lane detection. Default "main".

commitGuard.description: Default true: blocks `git commit` when the current diff has not been through /gate. It does not just fail — it hands the agent a reason, the agent asks you whether to review first or commit anyway, and 'anyway' arms a one-shot bypass (`lanes allow-commit`). Set false to disable; /gate still works when invoked directly.

largeDiffThreshold.description: Changed-line count past which the guard warns that review quality degrades. Default 400.

excludePattern.description: Regex of generated/vendored paths to drop from review scope. Reviewing them is pure noise.

domainAxes.description: THE field that decides whether the reviewer is worth running. Judgment axes on top of architecture/duplication/documentation currency, which the reviewer already checks for free — leave this empty and you get a reviewer that finds only what your linter already found. Test for an axis: a linter could not check it; if a rule can be mechanised, put it in lint config instead, where it runs in milliseconds. How to find yours: read the last 10-20 real review comments your team left on PRs, discard everything about formatting/naming — what's left, the comments that needed someone who knows this product, is your list. Write 3-4 sharp axes in your team's own words; each vague one dilutes the rest. Bad: 'Follow best practices', 'Code should be readable'. Good: 'Money paths: anything touching price, tax or discount must keep the calculation in one place and record the inputs it used. A second copy of the formula is a defect even when it agrees today.'

framework.description: Test framework name (e.g. "vitest", "pytest"), shown to the test-writer agent for context.

expertiseDoc.description: Repo-relative path to the project's testing conventions doc, read by the test agent before writing anything.

locationRule.description: Where new test files belong, in your own words (e.g. "Co-located as <name>.test.ts next to the unit under test.").

issueProvider.description: "github" needs `gh` authenticated (check with `gh auth status`) — /architect creates an issue and its linked branch. "none" skips that: /architect hands you the finished spec instead, and you file it wherever you actually track work.

specSections.description: Section headings /architect fills in, in order, when writing the spec.

challengeSpec.description: Run the spec-challenger agent against the draft spec before creating the issue. Default true.

dev.description: Per-lane dev services. Every project declares its own: no two stacks start the same way, and one repo can have several services (e.g. a React client and a Python API) with different commands, directories and port series. Started detached as process-group leaders, so `lanes stop` kills the whole tree. Omit this entirely and `lanes dev` just tells you nothing is declared — everything else still works.

name.description: Short id, used in `lanes dev` output, log filenames and `lanes logs <n> <name>`.

cwd.description: Directory relative to the worktree root. Default "." — set it for monorepo services.

portBase.description: Port prefix for this service. Lane N gets `${portBase}${N}` (400 -> lane 2 is 4002). Defaults to the top-level basePort. Per-machine overridable by service name via `lanes service-port <name> <n>`, same gitignored local file and same precedence as worktreesDir/basePort.

url.description: Optional URL for this service. Printed by `lanes dev` when it starts, and shown on the `lanes status` dashboard while it is running. Same placeholders.
